about: Where each text in data/regulations/text came from, and how it was read. chunks.jsonl is built from these files by `python -m src.regulations build`.

sources.title: The Drone Rules, 2021
sources.issuer: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
sources.instrument: G.S.R. 589(E), 25 August 2021 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3(i), No. 477)
sources.status: In force. The text here is the rules as first notified; the Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2022 and 2023 changed some wording, and each affected rule carries an editorial note saying what changed.
sources.source_note: A scan of the rules as printed in a compiled volume (pages 324 to 347), hosted on a court website. It is not the Gazette original. The Ministry's own rules page returned HTTP 403 to the tool used here, so the Gazette copy could not be compared word for word.
sources.method: The scanned pages were read by OCR, then every page was transcribed by reading the page image, with the OCR as a cross-check. The OCR misread clause labels and dropped lines, so the OCR text itself is not used. All 55 rules and the 5 forms are present and in order. The numbers (heights, distances, weights, periods, fees, penalty) were compared with the OCR reading of the same pages, and key provisions were checked against published summaries of the rules.
omitted: the blank answer cells of the forms (the list of fields is kept)
sources.licence_note: Subordinate legislation published in the Official Gazette. Reproduction of Gazette matter is generally permitted under section 52(1)(q) of the Copyright Act, 1957 (my reading, not legal advice).

annotations.note: clause (t) was substituted by the Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2022 (G.S.R. 108(E), 11 February 2022). It now reads: “Remote Pilot Certificate” means the certificate issued by an authorised remote pilot training organisation to any individual under rule 34.

by the Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2022 (G.S.R. 108(E)), Part VI is headed “REMOTE PILOT CERTIFICATE” and the word “licence” reads “certificate” wherever it occurs in it. The same applies to rules 32 to 36.
“licence” now reads “certificate”, and sub-rule (4) was omitted (Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2022, G.S.R. 108(E)).

sources.title: The Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2022
sources.issuer: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
sources.status: In force. Amends the Drone Rules, 2021.
sources.source_note: The Ministry's Gazette PDF. Its text layer is garbled, so the pages were read from the images.
sources.method: Page images read directly. The notification is bilingual and only the English text is transcribed.
sources.licence_note: Published in the Official Gazette; see the note on the Drone Rules, 2021.

sources.title: The Drone (Amendment) Rules, 2023
sources.issuer: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
sources.status: In force. Amends Form D-4 of the Drone Rules, 2021.
sources.source_note: The Ministry's copy has a corrupted text layer. The text was read from the same notification, which is the last page of the compiled volume of the Drone Rules, 2021 (sha256 793e6bba...c560, page 25 of the PDF).
sources.licence_note: Published in the Official Gazette; see the note on the Drone Rules, 2021.

sources.title: National Unmanned Aircraft System Traffic Management (UTM) Policy Framework, 2021
sources.issuer: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India
sources.status: A policy framework, not a rule. It describes the intended architecture and services for managing drone traffic at low altitude.
sources.source_note: The Ministry's PDF, which has a clean text layer.
sources.method: Text layer extracted and normalised by a one-off script (not kept in this repository):page numbers and the contents page removed, wrapped lines joined, and word breaks the PDF introduced ("airspa ce") repaired only where a dictionary confirmed the joined word. Headings and wording were then spot-checked.
omitted: Appendix I (a responsibility matrix, a table that does not survive text extraction)
sources.licence_note: A Government of India publication on a ministry website. Check the site's copyright policy before reusing it beyond research and study.

sources.title: FAA Aeronautical Information Manual, paragraph 5-1-3, Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) System
sources.short_title: FAA AIM 5-1-3 (United States guidance, not Indian law)
sources.instrument: AIM paragraph 5-1-3 as published on faa.gov on the retrieval date
sources.status: United States guidance. Included only because it explains what a NOTAM is and how its fields work. It is not Indian law.
sources.source_note: The whole Section 1 page; only paragraph 5-1-3 was kept.
sources.method: HTML parsed by a one-off script (not kept in this repository);the cross-reference boxes were dropped and the sub-paragraphs given their own headings.
sources.licence_note: A work of the United States government, so in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
